chunks: 41 - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub said:

A man wrote to the Faqih (peace be upon him): A man bequeathed to his mawali (clients/freemen) and the mawali of his father one-third of his wealth. When that was not reached (or when the bequest was executed), he said: 'The wealth belongs to his mawali, and the mawali of his father are excluded (their share is dropped).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a bequest to both one's own mawali and the mawali of one's father?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies the distinction between personal and paternal clientage (*mawali*) in inheritance law, affirming that a bequest to one's own mawali is valid while the father's mawali are excluded. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the bond of *mawali* is personal to the individual unless specified otherwise, ensuring the testator's intent is respected. The ruling underscores the precision required in distinguishing between different categories of dependents when executing a *wasiyya* (bequest).
